Website Architecture

Status: LIVE (static build) + PLANNED (interactive backend layer).

Edit this page on GitHub

Website Architecture

Status: LIVE (static build) + PLANNED (interactive backend layer). Source of truth: website/build.py + website/config/** + the docs/ corpus. Owner doc: this file.

This document describes how the Kaiteyo website actually works today, how the project command center fits in, and the contract the interactive backend must obey when it ships. It follows the corpus honesty rule: nothing on the site may claim a status the repository does not support (see docs/planning/CURRENT_STATE.md for the status vocabulary).

1. Current architecture (LIVE)

The website is a static site generated by a Python build (website/build.py). There is no server runtime, no database, and no authentication. Everything is rendered at build time from files in the repository.

text
docs/  (the corpus: architecture, engineering, product, game, planning, ...)
   │
   ▼
website/build.py  ── reads ──▶  website/config/*.json   (navigation, site, themes, ...)
   │                             website/content/**     (pages, wiki, FAQ, guides, ...)
   │
   ├── renders docs/ → /docs/**            (markdown → HTML)
   ├── renders content/ → /, /features/, /wiki/, ...
   ├── renders project/ → /project/**       (command center, from config/project/* + MASTER_TODO.md)
   │
   ▼
website/dist/**   (static HTML/CSS/JS — committed per current policy; see §7)

1.1 Key inputs

Input Purpose Edited by
docs/** The documentation corpus — one truth for everything the site says humans + AI agents
website/config/site.json Site metadata (name, version, tagline) humans
website/config/navigation.json Primary navigation groups humans
website/config/themes.json Theme gallery definitions humans
website/config/project/*.json Command-center data (systems, whiteboard, roadmap, suggestions, activity) humans/AI — with the honesty rules in §4
docs/planning/MASTER_TODO.md Kanban task source — parsed, not duplicated humans/AI
docs/architecture/decisions/*.md Decisions index — parsed, not duplicated humans/AI
website/content/** Page-level content (home, features, roadmap, wiki, FAQ, guides) humans

1.2 Build stages (build.py)

  1. copy_assets() — static assets (styles, scripts, icons, images) to dist/.
  2. build_documentation() — walks docs/ sections, renders markdown to HTML under /docs/, builds the per-section index and the docs landing page.
  3. build_faq(), build_shortcuts(), build_changelog(), build_wiki(), build_guides() — content-driven pages.
  4. build_pages() — top-level pages (/, /features/, /roadmap/, …).
  5. build_project() — the command center (see §2).
  6. build_trial() — the web trial page (/try/, a static slice).
  7. Search index assembly + global search page.

1.3 Templates

Jinja2, loaded from website/templates/. Layouts extend base.html; the project pages extend layouts/project.html (a shell with the section rail) and share macros in partials/project-macros.html (status badges, doc links).

2. The project command center (LIVE, read-only)

The website now includes a public project command center at /project/ with eight connected surfaces:

Surface Route Renders from Interaction
Project status /project/ systems.json + live counters links to docs/board
Kanban /project/kanban/ MASTER_TODO.md (parsed) client-side filter/search
Roadmap /project/roadmap/ roadmap.json links to docs + kanban package
Whiteboard /project/whiteboard/ whiteboard.json interactive pan/zoom/LOD canvas
Suggestions /project/suggestions/ suggestions.json + GitHub issues link workflow + template
Decisions /project/decisions/ docs/architecture/decisions/*.md (parsed) links to rendered ADR pages
Activity /project/activity/ activity.json (real snapshot) read-only feed
Contributing /project/contributing/ live task lists + package knowledge links to kanban items

2.1 Single source of truth rules

  1. Tasks come from docs/planning/MASTER_TODO.md. The build parses the table rows (ID, title, status, priority, deps, acceptance); the Kanban is a rendering of that file. Never edit kanban data anywhere else.
  2. Decisions come from docs/architecture/decisions/. The build parses the ADR headings; the Decisions page links to the rendered pages.
  3. System statuses come from systems.json, which mirrors docs/planning/CURRENT_STATE.md. When the repo status changes, update CURRENT_STATE.md and systems.json/roadmap.json together.
  4. Activity is a dated snapshot (activity.json). Its captured field records when it was taken; refreshing it is a documented procedure (§6).

2.2 Whiteboard behavior

whiteboard.js renders the graph from embedded JSON. Features:

  • Pan — pointer drag anywhere on the canvas.
  • Zoom — scroll wheel (pointer-anchored), +/− buttons, 0 = fit, +/−/0 keyboard shortcuts while the canvas is focused.
  • Semantic LOD — three levels as you zoom out: full detail (descriptions + status) → node labels only → groups only. Node kinds are color-coded by border (system/feature/database/API/integration/game); edges are typed and labeled (DEPENDS_ON, USES, PRODUCES, FEEDS, CONTAINS, …).
  • Click/Enter on a node opens its documentation in a new tab.
  • Minimap — fixed corner overview with the current viewport rectangle.

The board is read-only by design. Editing it requires the backend layer (§5, API.md).

3. Navigation

navigation.json defines four groups:

  • Learn — Try, Download, Product, Learn, Features, Screenshots, Theme Gallery.
  • Explore — Documentation, Wiki, Guides, Q&A, Keyboard Shortcuts, Product Roadmap, Changelog.
  • Command Center — Project Status, Kanban, Roadmap, Whiteboard, Suggestions, Architecture Decisions, Activity, Contributing.
  • Community — Integrations, Install, About, Community, Data & Attribution, Plugins, Credits, License, Privacy, Security.

Two roadmaps exist deliberately:

  • Product Roadmap (/roadmap/) — released/historical versions timeline.
  • Project Roadmap (/project/roadmap/) — forward-looking phases with status, linked to kanban packages and documentation. Each page links to the other.

4. Honesty rules (binding)

  1. Every status on the command center comes from the corpus status vocabulary: IMPLEMENTED, PARTIALLY_IMPLEMENTED, ARCHITECTED (target), PLANNED, PLACEHOLDER, BLOCKED, DONE, IN_PROGRESS, RESEARCH.
  2. ARCHITECTED/TARGET means fully designed, not built. The Journey nodes on the whiteboard are labeled Target; the roadmap page explains the label.
  3. No fabricated data: suggestions.json's item list stays empty until a real suggestions backend exists; activity.json only contains verified events (commits from git log, ADR dates, released versions).
  4. No fake interactivity: the kanban is filter-only; card moves, whiteboard edits, and suggestion submission are documented API contracts, never frontend simulations with silent success.
  5. Any page claiming a system is "live" must match CURRENT_STATE.md. When in doubt, downgrade the claim.

5. The interactive layer (PLANNED)

The command center surfaces were built to be upgraded in place. When the backend ships (see API.md and DATA_MODEL.md):

  • The same routes gain POST/PATCH endpoints; the static render remains the fallback (progressive enhancement, not replacement).
  • Tasks, decisions, systems, and roadmap items keep the corpus as the canonical write target where feasible (e.g. editing a task updates MASTER_TODO.md, then the board re-renders). Interactive-only data (comments, suggestions, activity) lives in the project database.
  • Realtime (WebSocket) is layered on the event bus described in API.md; the static pages never fake live updates.
  • Permissions are enforced server-side (see API.md §Security). The static site may show/hide nothing sensitive — it contains only public data.

6. Maintenance procedures

6.1 Regenerate the site

text
cd website
python3 build.py

Requires Python 3.10+ and the packages in website/requirements.txt.

6.2 Refresh the activity feed

  1. git log --oneline -20 for recent commits.
  2. Check docs/architecture/decisions/ for new ADRs and website/config/project/roadmap.json / docs/roadmap/ROADMAP.md for phase changes.
  3. Update activity.json (new events first, bump captured).
  4. Rebuild the site and verify the feed.

6.3 Add a system / roadmap item

  1. Update docs/planning/CURRENT_STATE.md (status) and docs/planning/MASTER_TODO.md (tasks) first.
  2. Mirror into systems.json / roadmap.json (id, label, status, docs link).
  3. If it belongs on the whiteboard, add the node (+ edges) to whiteboard.json and run the link check (§8).

6.4 Edit a kanban task status

Edit the row in docs/planning/MASTER_TODO.md (status/priority columns use the documented emoji/format) and rebuild. The board is a rendering.

7. Known limitations / debt

  • dist/ is committed (per current repo policy) — CI regeneration is the paydown; see docs/planning/TODO.md.
  • No Python in the authoring environment for some contributors; the build is plain stdlib + Jinja2 to keep the barrier low.
  • The whiteboard data file is hand-maintained JSON; node coordinates need care when adding nodes (use the fit button to sanity-check).
  • Suggestions/activity are snapshots or links until the backend ships.
  • GitHub is the issue tracker; the Suggestions page links issues rather than duplicating them.

8. Verification checklist (run after any change)

  1. node --check website/assets/scripts/*.js — JS syntax.
  2. JSON validity: python3 -m json.tool on each website/config/**/*.json.
  3. Link integrity: every href/docs link in the new templates resolves (relative links against the rendered output; run a crawl over dist/).
  4. Status labels: grep the rendered /project/ pages for any status word not in the corpus vocabulary (§4.1).
  5. No orphan documents: every new file is reachable from docs/README.md or a section index.
